content: This judgment from the Court of Lagonegro concerns a preliminary ruling on division of property between separated spouses involving land purchased in 1994 and a two-storey building constructed in 1995, currently used as a gym with adjoining football/tennis court and parking, all under legal community property regime. The plaintiff requested dissolution and division following judicial separation pronounced in 2013. The defendant appeared without opposing division but objected that the property complex was purchased with contributions from his family of origin, requesting suspension of proceedings due to pending litigation concerning repayment claims by his father, and noting that he operated his gym business within the property so no sale should be ordered. The court rejected the suspension request as there was no prejudicial relationship between the cases, and the other proceeding had been terminated for inactivity. The court held that pursuant to Article 191 of the Italian Civil Code as amended by Law 55/2015, legal community must be understood as dissolved upon authorization for spouses to live separately. The court noted that division judgment constitutes a petitory judgment requiring ascertainment of co-ownership or ownership of real right as necessary logical antecedent to final decision. Parties must provide evidence of co-ownership or joint ownership of real rights, and proof of ownership of immovable property cannot be provided by cadastral certificates, alleged acknowledgements, or deductive process, as written deed ad substantiam or equivalent fact such as adverse possession is necessary. The court found it documented that the property was purchased by the defendant spouse under legal community regime and is included pursuant to Articles 177 and 178 of the Italian Civil Code in the legal community property of the spouses, as confirmed by notarial certification and technical report. The court therefore ascertained the property falls within legal community, declared dissolution of joint ownership with effect from April 30, 2012 (date of authorization to live separately), and returned the case to preliminary hearing stage for continuation of division proceedings, with costs to be determined at final hearing.
